questions.question: An older man with COPD (or, in the pediatric exam, a 26-week-old infant) presents with an upper respiratory tract infection after contact with a 2-year-old who had a cold.
questions.question_raw: Q1 (2012 PM). URTI in old guy with COPD (or a 26 week old baby in peds exam) in contact with a 2 year old who had a cold

parts.text: Name a diagnostic test that will give a result within 24 hours.
List six viruses that could cause this presentation.

parts_raw.text: a) Diagnostic test will give result within 24h

questions.model_answer:
a) Respiratory multiplex PCR assay — these assays test for more than 20 respiratory viruses and bacteria simultaneously and are used on wards and in the ED to guide treatment, returning results rapidly (within 24h); they are not indicated for the typical uncomplicated cold.
b) Any six of the viruses associated with the common cold (Table 58.1): (1) Rhinovirus (2) Coronavirus (3) Parainfluenza virus (4) Respiratory syncytial virus (5) Influenza virus (6) Adenovirus. (Human metapneumovirus, enteroviruses, and bocavirus are also recognized causes.)

cohort_answer.text: a) PCR respiratory multiplex (within 24h, covers many pathogens); culture is most sensitive but takes days; antigen detection is fastest but limited (as for influenza A/B); serologic methods also exist. Viruses: SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, Parainfluenza, Rhinovirus, Adenovirus, Enterovirus, RSV, Human metapneumovirus, OC43, bocavirus (mnemonic RAPIER: rhino, adeno, paraflu, influenza, entero, RSV, + COVID; coronaviruses more common than enterovirus).
